unit.title: AI security policy and red teaming at school

video.title: When AI goes wrong
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — university lecturer in education, Bangladesh (main character)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: A voice note she never sent

scenes.visual: Cards: The head's “voice note”; Fees due today; She never recorded it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: At eight on a Monday, a voice note from the head teacher went round the parents' group. School closed, it said, and fees due today by mobile money. The head teacher was at her desk. She had never recorded it.

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how a school responds when AI goes wrong, step by step.

scenes.visual: A list: Data pasted into a public tool; A fake of a teacher or pupil; Harmful advice from a chatbot; An agent acting without a yes.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: What counts as an AI incident
scenes.narration: AI incidents at school come in a few kinds. Personal data pasted into a public tool. A fake of a teacher or a pupil. A chatbot giving harmful advice. Or an agent that acted without anyone's yes.

scenes.visual: A list: Stop the tool or the post; Change passwords; Warn on a trusted channel; Support anyone targeted.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: When one happens, act in order. First, contain it: stop the tool, ask for the post to come down, change the password. Then protect people: warn parents on the channel they already trust, and support anyone targeted.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Next, keep the evidence without spreading it: note the time, the sender and where it appeared. Report it to your school's lead, and to the provider. And if personal data leaked, many laws expect the regulator to hear within seventy-two hours.

scenes.visual: A list: What let it happen?; Fix the cause; A code word for money; Tell every family.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The last step is the one schools skip. Ask what let it happen, and fix that, not just the symptom. After our voice-note scare, we agreed a code word for any money request, and told every family.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A teacher tells you she pasted a class list with health notes into a public chatbot an hour ago. What's the first step?

scenes.visual: Cards: Delete it, training off; The data lead decides; Thank her.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Contain it: delete the chat and its history, and turn training off. Then the data lead decides who must be told. And thank the teacher: if people are blamed, the next mistake stays hidden.

scenes.visual: A list: A 20-minute drill each term; Staff decide each step; Pupils: stop, don't share, tell.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Don't wait for the real thing. Run a twenty-minute drill each term: read out an incident and let staff decide each step. Then teach pupils the short version: stop, don't share it, tell a trusted adult.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: Eight messages; Real or scam?; Report to whom?; Perfect spelling.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, eight messages arrive by text, chat and email, some real and some scams. Use them as a drill: for each one, decide, then say what you'd report and to whom. Notice that the scams have perfect spelling.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A fake picture of a pupil is spreading in a class group. Who do we help first?

scenes.visual: The summary: Contain it; Protect people; Evidence and report; Learn and fix the cause. Takeaway: Practise the response before you need it.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: The pupil in the picture comes first. Remember: contain it, protect people, keep evidence and report, then learn and fix the cause.

scenes.visual: A list: A 20-minute staff drill; The fake voice-note story; Each table decides; Pin the steps up.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Try it at school this week
scenes.narration: Try it at school this week: run a twenty-minute drill at a staff meeting. Read out the fake voice-note story and let each table decide the steps. Write the agreed steps on one card, and pin it up in the staffroom.

checkpoints.prompt: A teacher pasted a class list with health notes into a public chatbot an hour ago. What's the first step?

options.text: Wait and see if anything happens
Contain it: delete the chat and its history, and tell the data lead
Blame her in the staff group

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes: contain it now, then report. And thank her for telling you.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: contain it first, then report. Blame makes people hide mistakes.

checkpoints.prompt: A fake picture of a pupil is spreading in a class group. Who do you help first?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes: the person harmed comes first. Then stop it spreading and follow the procedure.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: protect the person harmed first; the rest follows the procedure.
